data.hypothesis: The valid 16x32 output tile with K depth 32 measured 0.0228994 s, while the valid coalesced untiled control measured 0.0234084 s. This contrasting 32x16 output tile with K depth 16 keeps one output per thread and contiguous column segments, while halving the shared-memory tile footprint; it also narrows each warp's column span, reverses operand reuse, and doubles K-loop iterations. Correctness and repeated timing will test that tradeoff without assuming a speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as a comparison baseline for this narrower-column, smaller-K-depth CTA tile; the three-sample measurements do not establish a repeatable cause or gain.
memory_lessons.claim: The coalesced control was valid at 0.0234084123 s mean over three samples; the 16x32, K-depth-32 tiled candidate was valid at 0.0228994478 s mean over three samples. The difference is small and remains an observed comparison, not proof that tiling improves performance.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this contrasting 32x16, K-depth-16 candidate with the same correctness checks and repeated-timing protocol, then compare its samples and correctness to both valid candidates.

data.notes: This proposal has not been compiled, correctness-checked, or timed. It preserves the run entry point, default-stream launch, buffers, and alpha/beta update; it uses no additional allocations or external math library. The controller should determine correctness and repeated performance.
transformations: Replaced the baseline kernel with a 32-row by 16-column output tile and a K depth of 16, contrasting with the measured 16x32, K-depth-32 tile.
Mapped each thread to one output; threadIdx.x spans the 16 output columns and threadIdx.y spans 32 rows.
Cooperatively staged A and B tiles into shared memory with synchronous barriers, zero-filled K and matrix tails, and used a guarded K-loop increment.

Used size_t for matrix element offsets and quotient/remainder grid calculations; retained the run signature, default-stream launch, alpha/beta semantics, and unused scratch parameter without adding allocations or libraries.
